rounds.text: Creative Newtech Ltd is demonstrating exceptional fundamental momentum, evidenced by a compounded profit growth of 45% over five years and a 36% expansion over the trailing twelve months [E17, E19]. This top-tier operational performance is further reinforced by strong top-line delivery, featuring a 39% five-year compounded sales growth rate and a 49% surge over the trailing twelve months [E14, E16]. The company generates returns well ahead of its peers, boasting an ROCE of 18.8% and a median return on equity of 21% over the last five years, dwarfing respective sector benchmarks of 6.61% and 5.09% [E10, E13, E23]. Market participants appear to be mispricing this earnings power because a discounted cash flow model establishes an intrinsic value of Rs 2002 per share against a market price of Rs 1155, leaving a substantial 42.3% margin of safety [E41, E42]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF indicates that today's price only assumes a modest 10.4% earnings growth, which is easily cleared by the base case expectation of 18.0% growth [E43]. Institutional backing is quietly expanding, generating positive institutional money flow alongside a rules-based screening score of 96 out of 100 carrying a high-confidence buy designation [E40, E58]. Conceded: the business carries negative operating cash flow of Rs -272 Cr for Mar 2026 alongside rising debtor days [E31, E57].

Creative Newtech Ltd carries severe underlying financial risks that the headline growth metrics obscure. Most alarming is the company's cash generation collapse, evidenced by operating cash flow plunging to Rs -272 Cr and free cash flow dropping to Rs -275 Cr in Mar 2026, resulting in an abysmal cash conversion ratio of -3.89x against reported profit [E30, E32]. This severe cash burn has coincided with a massive surge in borrowings from Rs 72 Cr to Rs 324 Cr in just one year [E35], while debtor days have deteriorated significantly from 52.0 to 76.3 days [E57]. Furthermore, valuation multiples trade at a clear premium to sector benchmarks, with a P/E of 22.77x versus the sector's 18.85x, a P/B of 4.61x against 1.39x, and an EV/EBITDA of 17x compared to 10.49x [E6, E7, E11]. The equity also exhibits high historical risk, carrying an annualized volatility of 52.6% and a worst peak-to-trough drawdown of -51.3% [E49, E50]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong historical compound sales and profit growth over three and five-year periods alongside an ROE of 18.8% [E13, E17, E18].

Conceded: operating cash flow dropped to Rs -272 Cr and free cash flow to Rs -275 Cr in Mar 2026 [E30, E32], and borrowings rose to Rs 324 Cr alongside lengthening debtor days [E35, E57]. However, the bear's valuation critique ignores that a discounted cash flow model places intrinsic value at Rs 2002 per share, leaving a substantial margin of safety of 42.3% [E41, E42]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF indicates that the current market price only implies a 10.4% earnings growth rate, which is easily cleared by the company's historical 5-year profit growth of 45% and trailing twelve-month profit growth of 36% [E17, E19, E43]. While the stock trades at sector-relative premiums, its fundamental profitability utterly dominates sector benchmarks, delivering an ROE of 18.8% and an ROCE of 14.89% against sector medians of 5.09% and 6.61% respectively [E7, E9, E10, E13]. Finally, institutional sentiment completely rejects the notion of fundamental weakness, displaying positive institutional money flow alongside rising domestic and foreign institutional shareholdings [E38, E39, E40].

The bull’s reliance on a DCF model [E41] ignores the reality that the company’s cash generation has collapsed, with operating cash flow turning negative to Rs -272 Cr [E31] and free cash flow to Rs -275 Cr [E32]. While the bull points to historical profit growth [E17, E19], this is disconnected from the current financial reality where cash conversion is a staggering -3.89x [E30] and borrowings have surged from Rs 72 Cr to Rs 324 Cr in a single year [E35]. Conceded: the company has delivered strong historical profit growth [E56]. However, the bull’s claim that current pricing is conservative [E43] fails to account for the fact that the stock is already trading at a significant premium to its sector in both P/E [E6] and P/B [E7], while simultaneously facing a deterioration in working capital efficiency as debtor days have climbed to 76.3 [E57]. Furthermore, the bull’s focus on institutional sentiment [E38, E39, E40] ignores the high annualised volatility of 52.6% [E50] and the historical risk of a -51.3% peak-to-trough drawdown [E49], which suggests that the current valuation leaves little room for error should the recent inconsistent quarterly margins [E29] fail to stabilize.

The bear’s focus on negative cash flow [E31, E32] ignores the company’s structural growth trajectory, where sales have compounded at 39% over five years [E14] and 49% in the TTM [E16], necessitating aggressive capital deployment. Conceded: cash conversion is currently -3.89x [E30] and borrowings have increased [E35]. However, this expansion is clearly yielding results, as evidenced by an ROE of 18.8% [E13] and an ROCE of 14.89% [E10], both of which significantly outperform sector benchmarks [E9, E10]. While the bear highlights the premium P/E and P/B [E6, E7], these multiples are justified by the company’s superior profitability, with an ROA of 7.86% compared to the sector’s 2.86% [E8]. The concern regarding debtor days [E57] is mitigated by the fact that the company is currently in a high-growth phase, supported by positive institutional money flow [E40] and a high relative-strength rating of 100 [E47]. Finally, the bear’s emphasis on volatility [E50] overlooks the fact that the stock is currently trading above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E46], reflecting strong market confidence in the underlying fundamentals.

The bull attempts to brush off negative cash flow as mere structural growth, but an operating cash flow of Rs -272 Cr and free cash flow of Rs -275 Cr in Mar 2026 are severe operational drains, not routine accounting adjustments [E31, E32]. Conceded: sales have compounded at 39% over 5 years and 49% in the TTM [E14, E16], but this expansion has simultaneously caused borrowings to balloon from Rs 72 Cr to Rs 324 Cr in a single year alongside a sharp deterioration in debtor days from 52.0 to 76.3 [E35, E57]. While the bull points to strong returns on equity and capital employed to justify valuation multiples, the data provider shows that the company trades at a steep P/E of 22.77x, P/B of 4.61x, and EV/EBITDA of 17x—all sitting at significant premiums to their respective sector benchmarks [E6, E7, E11]. Furthermore, the bull's dismissal of volatility ignores that the stock carries a high annualized volatility of 52.6% alongside a historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -51.3%, proving that the price action is prone to severe structural collapses [E49, E50]. Finally, the claim of consistent operating performance is undermined by the evidence that quarterly operating margins are "Inconsistent" over the last three quarters, while recent price growth outpaces profit growth by 54%, signaling that market expectations have far outrun underlying delivery [E29, E53].
